q: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called vaporization.
e: True. The process of changing liquid into vapour is called vaporization. process has to stay in that role in the sentence.

q: The temperature at which a liquid vapourizes under normal pressure is called its boiling point.
e: True. The temperature at which a liquid vapourizes under normal pressure is called its boiling point. Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column.

q: Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the specific latent heat of vaporization $L_v$ of the liquid.
e: True. Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the specific latent heat of vaporization L_v of the liquid. Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is $2\ 255\ 176 \ J kg^{-1}$.
e: True. The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is 2 255 176 J kg^-1. Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature.

q: But $2.255 \times 10^6 \ J kg^{-1}$ will be assumed for simplicity in calculations.
e: True. But 2.255 × 10^6 J kg^-1 will be assumed for simplicity in calculations. 1 kW = 10³ W and 1 MW = 10⁶ W.

q: The change of vapour (or) gas phase into liquid phase is called condensation.
e: True. The change of vapour (or) gas phase into liquid phase is called condensation. change has to stay in that role in the sentence.

q: In condensation, the substance absorbs heat.
e: False. The claim puts absorbs where releases belongs. In condensation, the substance releases heat. Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference.
